Commentary.Commentary: That concludes the opening encounter of this All-Asian Triangular T20I series. The hosts began on the right note, getting the better of their Asian neighbors. Next up, Bangladesh and India face each other at the same venue. That clash is on International Women's Day. See you at 1900 local time (1330 GMT) then. Till then, take care! Adios amigos!

Dinesh Chandimal, the glee-looking captain, is elated to win against India after 7 games. Says that this is a good start for the tourney and the signs of things to come from them. Adds about taking this confidence going forward. About having a spring in his step in the game, he plays it down saying that the entire team gelled well and that made it easier for him. Praises their coach as well as the management for this win. After the chat, he goes on to take the match winner's trophy from the presentation panel.

Rohit Sharma, the glum-faced skipper, states that they ended up with a par score and something that was enough to play with. Adds that some more acceleration was desirable towards the end with the bat. Concedes that the start that Sri Lanka got was instrumental in them gunning this total down. Reckons that sometimes things can go wrong and sounds hopeful of his boys learning from this outing. Mentions of having enough experience in their bowling line-up. He states that although the international experience is less, their bowlers are pretty well-exposed to the format and hence the management backs them to do the task. Iterates about having a good depth in the side. Ends vowing to come back stronger in the next games.

The Man of the Match tonight is Kusal Perera for his belligerent knock. He begins by stating that this was his best innings. Reckons that after injuring himself, he went and played at the club level and got himself ready to the rigors of international cricket. Ends saying that the target was a stiff one but they were confident of chasing this down.

The Indian bowling came cropper tonight. Apart from the most-economical-of-the-lot Washington Sundar, who picked up a couple of wickets, the others disappeared to all parts of the ground. Yuzvendra Chahal also had two to his name, but he was a tad too expensive. That Shardul Thakur over of 27 runs was perhaps signs of things to come for the Indians tonight. That meant that Shikhar Dhawan's 90 went in vain. Let's see what the captains and the player of the match have to say...

The others just had to chip in to mark their attendance after the 58-run partnership between Perera and Danushka Gunathilaka. The final rites were done by the twin all-rounder pair of Thisara Perera and Dasun Shanaka. They quelled any hopes of an Indian win in the series opener.

The hosts were on the money right from the outset. Their initial burst of 75 runs in the first 6 overs, their best in a T20I, helped them steamroll the opponents. Kusal Perera had the lion's share in the exploits. He smashed a quickfire 66 and that set the platform for them. They never looked back from that.

Sri Lanka, for a change, have got the better of the Indians in an international game! Yes, these words are rare to see. What stamps the odd nature of win is this - this is the first time India have lost a T20I against Sri Lanka at the R Premadasa Stadium in Colombo.

FOUR! Those are the winning runs! Thisara Perera's blade brings them. This is short in length, Perera pulls it through backward square leg. The ball speeds away to the fence, beating square leg to his left and fine leg to his right. SRI LANKA REGISTER THE FIRST WIN IN THE TRI-SERIES, A 5-WICKET WIN WITH 9 BALLS TO SPARE!
Short in length, pulled away through mid-wicket for a brace. Just one hit away are the hosts from a win.
Full outside off, driven through covers for one.
WIDE! This is sprayed down the leg side, Shanaka misses the flick.
Shardul Thakur to bowl the penultimate over. Will he be able to take the game to the last over?

FOUR! 10 runs off the last two balls and that should seal the deal for Sri Lanka. This is a low full toss on the stumps, Perera thumps it straight over the non-striker and holds the pose. The ball bounces just in front of the ropes and that brings down the runs required to 8 off the last two overs.

SIX! Telling blow? Full on off, Perera gets his front leg out of the way and smites it straight over long off. The ball clears the fence easily. Sri Lankans needed just one big over and this is the one it seems.
WIDE! Full and well outside off, Perera fails to reach that. The umpire stretches his arms, that doesn't please the bowler one bit.
Another length ball, Shanaka comes down the track but fails to get bat on his attempted pull. The ball goes off his hips to the off side for a leg bye.
On a length on the stumps, Dasun misses his attempted pull.
FOUR! Shanaka belts this one! Length ball at a normal pace this time. Shanaka backs away and flat-bats it over covers for a boundary. Crucial one, as more 20 runs are needed off 16 balls.
Unadkat comes from round the wicket and delivers a slow length ball. Dasun makes room to slash it but is deceived by the change of pace.
Jaydev Unadkat to bowl his third over.
Length ball, flat-batted aerially to long off for a single. Shankar has bowled well here, 4 couples and a couple of singles, apart from a wide.
Short and wide outside off, slashed over point for another two.
Full and outside off, Shanaka slices it over backward point for a brace.
BEAMER! NOT A NO BALL, STRANGELY! Shanaka heaves it towards fine leg for a couple. All eyes are on the umpires but no signal from them. Lucky Shankar?
WIDE! This is full and outside off, Shanaka doesn't bother playing at that.
Full in length, Perera gets it off the bottom half of the blade over the bowler for one.

Trisection! Shankar runs in from round the wicket and hurls it full outside off, Perera looks to go over covers but ends up slicing it. Chahal runs back from covers, long off runs to his right and sweeper comes a bit to his left. But the ball lands in the centre of them and enables a brace.
Vijay Shankar to bowl the 17th over. Right call? Our colleague here, Parth, doesn't seem to agree.

Excellent over from Thakur comes to an end as just 3 came off this. This is banged short yet again, Shanaka is unable to slash it. 35 from 24 needed. The Lankans are 6 runs ahead than where India were at this point.
This ball is pushed through mid-wicket for one.

Back of a length delivery again, Shanaka plays this a la a forehand shot in tennis. Seems to have got it off the toe end towards long on for one. Shanaka seems to be hurt, as he seems to crouch after taking that run.
OUCH! That would have hurt. Thakur hurls a short length ball on the stumps, Dasun fails to pull that and gets hit on the hip.
Length ball outside off, pushed towards covers for nothing.
Short in length, Perera pulls it through mid-wicket for one.
Thisara opens his account with a punch through covers.
Floated on the stumps, defended off the front foot.
Thisara Perera is the next batter in for Sri Lanka. Though the card says 39 off 32 required, with two new batsmen in the middle, it could be anybody's game. A slip in place now.

OUT! Woodwork! This is flatter on a length around off, Tharanga hangs on the back foot and looks to heave it over the on side. Ends up missing the ball and finds his off stump pegged back. Chahal has this wonderful character of striking when the attack is on him. Does exactly the same now.
Flighted ball on the stumps, wristed to the on side for one.
This time a lofted shot over mid-wicket is played for a single.
Wrong 'un outside off on a shorter length, Upul cuts it in front of point for a brace.
Yuzvendra Chahal is back.

Length ball on the pads, Tharanga fails to get bat and the ball falls down after striking him on the pads. Shanaka calls him through for a single and makes it. A leg bye it is. Meanwhile, a funny thing happens. Karthik expects a kick from Thakur while the bowler expects the keeper to bend and collect it. Neither does anything and that takes Dinesh by surprise.

CHANCE DOWN! Rishabh Pant, the name which is associated with this one. This is short in length, Tharanga is hurried into the pull. Ends up getting it off the high end of the bat towards mid-wicket. Pant leaps full stretch to his right and gets a hand to it but fails to hold on. The ball rolls towards long on and a couple of runs are taken. Perhaps another fielder with a taller height could have done better.
Full on middle and leg, driven down to long on for one.
Short in length, pulled away through mid-wicket for one.
Length ball angling in, Tharanga has a swipe across the line but misses.
Thakur runs in from round the wicket and lands it on a length. Upul blocks.
Shardul Thakur is brought on after his sole over went for 27.
This one is pushed to the left of the bowler for nothing. Excellent stuff from Sundar - 4-0-28-2.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated on off, pushed towards covers.
Dasun Shanaka walks in next. The platform is set for him to get himself in and see his side through.

OUT! Is this the wicket that turns it around for India? Sundar is the man, who has provided the breakthrough for them. This is floated outside off, Perera comes down the track in search of a big shot. Misses the ball completely and Dinesh Karthik does the rest. This is exceptional stuff from the youngster, considering that he is bowling at a time when the batters are in a murderous mood. 48 more needed off 45 balls.
WIDE! Fired down leg, Perera fails to make contact with that.
Flatter trajectory on the pads, Kusal misses the flick and wears it on the pads.
Floated around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Washington Sundar to bowl out. 3-0-27-1 are his current figures.
Floated outside off, Tharanga chips it inside out over covers for a couple.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
This is eased down to long off for a single.
Flatter outside off, cut away through point for one.

SIX! Kusal Perera is audacious. Period. Raina darts it around off, it comes at a good length for Perera. He gets into position early and reverse hits it high and handsome over deep backward point for a biggie.
Tharanga drives it to long off for one.
Flatter outside off, punched through covers for one. 61 off 54 needed.
SIX! What a way to get off the mark. Tossed up delivery outside off, it is the leg spinner. Tharanga picks it up and smites it over deep mid-wicket for half a dozen.
Kusal slinks down the track and pushes it past the bowler for one.

FOUR! Ahhh! The Indians shouldn't be complaining about such type of runs as Dhawan also got them this way. This is floated down leg, Perera looks to sweep. Gets a top edge and the ball goes through to the fine leg fence.
This one is hit back to the bowler. Chahal gets low to his left but parries it away. It is a dot ball though.
WIDE! This is the googly but well outside off. Perera goes to the off side but fails to cut it. Wide given.
STOPPED! Floated on the stumps, Perera charges down and blasts it straight. Chahal stretches his right hand out and stops it cleanly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. Good over from Raina.
The batsman has driven it through mid off. The batsmen have run through for a single.
The ball hits the pads of Tharanga and they run through for one.
Another dot ball. Good bowling from Raina. Tharanga pushes this to covers.
The batsman has driven it through mid off.
Perera cuts this ball past point for a run.
Suresh Raina is into the attack.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
Upul Tharanga walks in next.

OUT! Chahal gets the skipper. Beautifully bowled by the spinner. Quicker through the air and Chandimal charges down the wicket but ends up yorking himself. Tries to flick it on the leg side but leaves a gap between bat and pad which is enough for the ball to go through and disturb the furniture.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. They manage to come back for the second.
FOUR! Good looking shot from the skipper. Seen the ball tossed up, he dances down to hit it past the bowler towards long off for a boundary.
Wrong'un. Chandimal gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Outside off, Chandimal looks to cut it but gets a top edge to it.
Good bouncer from Shankar to end the over. Outside off, Perera leaves it alone.
Chandimal pushes this through covers for one.
Bowls this at the ribs of Perera who pulls this to square leg for just one.
Perera shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
The ball takes an inside edge of the blade of Chandimal and they run through.
8th T20I fifty for Perera. This one is punched towards covers. Rohit dives to his left and parries it to his left. A run is eventually taken. Kusal has taken the attack to India here.
Vijay Shankar to bowl for the first time on his debut.
Outside off, Chandimal cuts it past point for a brace.
Perera hits it through mid-wicket for a single.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. A misfield there helps them come back for two.
SIX! No stopping Perera even after he lost his partner in the last over. Chahal tosses this in line of the stumps and Perera charges down and deposits this over the bowler's head for a maximum.
Chandimal drives this through mid off to rotate strike.
Spins this into Perera who eases it on the leg side for one.
Yuzvendra Chahal to roll his arm.
Flatter on the pads, turned to mid-wicket for nothing. Sri Lanka's best Powerplay in T20Is - 75/2. They are on course to chase the target in front of them.
Quick run this time. Kusal taps this one towards mid on again and this time quickly gets to the other end.
Flatter on off, Perera goes back and punches it to mid on for back-to-back dots.
Floated on middle, hit straight to mid on.
Flatter outside off, punched through covers for three runs.
Perera wrists this through mid-wicket for a single.
Dinesh Chandimal is next to bat.

OUT! One too many! India get the breakthrough. Slow ball in line of the stumps and Gunathilaka looks to go downtown. He is undone by the pace on that and ends up chipping it in the air. The ball goes towards mid off and Pant gets under it and takes a simple catch. A good catch to end the mayhem. A quickfire 58-run partnership for Sri Lanka comes to an end. Will India sneak through the line-up now?
FOUR! On the pads of Gunathilaka who works it down the leg side for a boundary.
Wide. The batsman tries flicking a ball that is down the leg side. Wide signalled by the umpire.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
SIX! Gunathilaka gets into the act now. Pitched up ball and he lofts it over mid on for half a dozen. Sri Lanka are on a roll.
Hits it well over mid-wicket and they come back for the second.
Perera gets an inside edge onto his pads and they scamper for the run. The fielder has a shy at the stumps but misses.
Jaydev Unadkat back for his second over.
SIX! It's raining in Colombo. No, not bad news, as it's raining sixes! This is tossed up around middle, Danushka gets down on a knee and smites it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
Angled in from round the wicket, chipped aerially towards mid on for a single.
Perera gets down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket. Before the throw from the deep comes in, a couple results. Excellent running.
Darted on the pads, Danushka fails to flick it away. The ball rolls away and a leg bye is taken.
Flatter on off, defended with a straight bat towards the bowler.
Dot ball. Thakur gets away. Bowls this short and Perera pulls it away only to find the short fine leg fielder.
FOUR! Straight back the bowler. Full again and Perera hits it down the ground past the bowler for another boundary. He is looking dangerous. 27 runs off this over with a ball to go.

FOUR! And to make matters worse it is a no-ball for height. Expensive over this from Thakur and he just cannot find the right length. Full toss this time and Perera carves it past point for the fourth boundary of the over. Free Hit coming up.
Shikhar Dhawan, the vice-captain, has something to say and he whispers his ideas to the skipper Rohit Sharma. Will this stop the bleeding?
SIX! All the way this time. Similar delivery and this time Perera gets plenty on it to go all the way for a maximum. 18 from the first four balls.
FOUR! Hat-trick of boundaries for Perera. Pitched up and Perera lofts it over mid off for four more.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for Perera. This is on a length and angling away. Perera uses the pace of Thakur and guides it towards point. Raina there dives to his left and gets some hand to hit. Chahal chases it down from covers, yet a boundary results.
FOUR! Starts off with a short ball and Perera pulls this behind square for a boundary.
Shardul Thakur to bowl his first over.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
SIX! Sweet! What a hit from Perera who has just come to bat. Tossed up and Perera gets low to sweep it over mid-wicket for a biggie!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Kusal Perera walks in next to bat.

OUT! India get an early wicket. Sundar is not afraid to toss the ball up even after getting hit for a boundary. He does so and deceives Mendis in the flight. Kusal looks to play a big shot over the on side and ends up skewing it off the outer half towards mid off. Dhawan there, backtracks and pouches it safely. Excellent bowling by the youngster and Mendis has to walk back early.
Gives this one air too and Mendis sweeps this behind square for a brace.
FOUR! First of the innings for Sri Lanka! Tossed up ball and Mendis chips it over mid off for a boundary.
Washington Sundar will share the new ball from the other end.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. Six runs from the first over.
Mendis gets this past covers for one.
FOUR! ALMOST a wicket for India. Length ball moving away from Mendis. He looks to cut this but the ball flies off the edge past Raina at first slip for a boundary.
Angles this away from Mendis who gets a bottom edge to it.
Length ball this time and Gunathilaka flicks it off his pads to pick up the first run of the innings.
Steams in and bowls it full. Gunathilaka stays in the crease and bunts this.

We are back for the chase. The umpires come out once again with the Indian players this time. Kusal Mendis and Danushka Gunathilaka will face the new ball. Jaydev Unadkat will start proceedings for the Indian team. One slip in place. Here we go...
